name: Cheese Stuffed Italian Sausage and Peppers Bake

prose.intro_html: Stuffed peppers usually means hollowing out a bell pepper and packing it full. This one flips the idea on its head, and honestly it is the easier road. You cut a slit in an Italian sausage, tuck a stick of mozzarella inside, and lay it on a bed of sliced peppers and onions. Marinara goes over the top, shredded cheese finishes it, and the oven does the rest of the work. Five minutes of real effort and it walks itself to done. Built at 14 servings it runs about {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein a serving, with under 15 grams of carbs. That is a hearty, cheesy dinner that stays inside your macros and does not ask much of you or your wallet.
shop_smart: Fourteen Italian sausage links are the whole plan, about four and a quarter pounds. One link per serving, so the protein portions itself with no math. Hot or mild is your call. They cost the same and cook the same, so buy whichever your table likes.

Fourteen sticks of mozzarella string cheese go inside the sausages. One stick tucked into each link is what melts through the middle as it bakes. Plain low moisture mozzarella sticks are all you need, not the flavored kind.

About a pound and a half of bell peppers make the bed, roughly five medium. Any color works here, so grab whatever red, yellow, green or orange looks good and is priced right. Buy them loose rather than in a shrink wrapped tray and you pay for peppers, not packaging.
Three onions round out the bed. They cook down sweet under the sausage and stretch the vegetables across all fourteen servings. A plain yellow onion is the budget staple and does the job.

Marinara and shredded mozzarella tie it together. The batch uses about two and three quarter cups of sauce and the same of shredded cheese. Store brand marinara behaves the same once it hits a hot oven, and any bag of shredded mozzarella melts fine over the top.
make_it: Heat the oven to 400 degrees. This batch fills two 9 by 13 baking pans, so pull both out now. Slice the onions and the bell peppers into strips and spread them in an even layer across the two pans. That bed is what each sausage bakes on top of.
Cut a slit down the length of each sausage, about halfway through, and leave the casing on. Do not cut all the way through. Tuck one string cheese stick into each slit.
Nestle the sausages cheese side up on the bed of peppers and onions, seven to a pan. Spoon the marinara over the sausages and vegetables, splitting it evenly between the two pans.
Bake for 30 to 40 minutes, until a thermometer pushed into the middle of a sausage reads 160 degrees. The peppers and onions will have softened down in the sauce underneath.
Scatter the shredded mozzarella over the top and return the pans to the oven for about 5 minutes, until the cheese is melted and bubbling.
Portion one stuffed sausage into each of your 14 containers, then spoon an even share of the peppers, onions and sauce over the top, about a heaping half cup each. That is the whole batch, done.
prose.portion_html: The honest way to fourteen even servings is the easy way here: one stuffed sausage per container portions the protein for you, no scale required. Then divide the peppers, onions and sauce evenly over the top, about a heaping half cup each, or weigh the bed and split it by the gram if you want it exact. Every serving lands near {{cal}} calories with {{protein}} grams of protein.
prose.cost_closing_html: About ${{cost_ps}} a serving at everyday prices for a cheesy, filling sausage dinner you can eat all week. The sausage carries the protein and the peppers and onions stretch it into fourteen full plates.

head.description: Cheese stuffed Italian sausage baked on a bed of peppers and onions with marinara and melted mozzarella, built for 14 servings. About {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein per serving, with under 15 grams of carbs.
head.keywords: italian sausage stuffed peppers, cheese stuffed sausage, low carb sausage and peppers, high protein meal prep, keto sausage bake
steps: Slice the onions and bell peppers and spread them in an even layer across two baking pans.
Cut a slit halfway into each sausage, tuck a mozzarella string cheese stick inside, and set them cheese side up on the vegetables.
Spoon marinara over the sausages and vegetables and bake at 400 degrees for 30 to 40 minutes, until the sausage reaches 160 degrees.
Scatter shredded mozzarella on top and bake about 5 more minutes until melted.
Portion one stuffed sausage per container with an even share of the peppers, onions and sauce.
